issues.description: The problem statement asks students to implement a function named _make_y_state (with a leading underscore) while the template and solution repositories use make_y_state (no underscore). This name/signature mismatch is structural: students following the problem text may implement _make_y_state and find the provided template/tests expect make_y_state, causing confusion or failing tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the function name consistent across all artifacts. Either update the problem statement and tests to refer to make_y_state (no underscore) or rename the template/solution function to _make_y_state. Ensure the documented signature (parameters and return) is identical in problem text, template stubs, and tests.

issues.description: The problem statement refers to the resource-state preparation function as `_make_y_state(...)` (leading underscore), while both the template and solution repositories define and use `make_y_state(...)` (no underscore). This naming mismatch can confuse students about which function to implement and expect in the starter code and tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the function reference in the problem statement from `_make_y_state` to `make_y_state` so the documented API matches the template and solution (and the tests). Alternatively, rename the template/solution function to `_make_y_state`, but aligning the problem text to `make_y_state` is recommended.
